solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Short lawyer gets long case

blocks.note: a clipped form of attorney
to long or yearn for something

explanation.surface: A lawyer of modest height is handed a lengthy court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is the verb meaning to yearn, not an adjective describing the case.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a slim briefcase for documents, short for attaché case.

clue.text: Nursemaid hugging son after hot bath is a charmer

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap arms round, so the nursemaid's letters enclose what follows

blocks.note: variant spelling of ayah, an Indian nursemaid
a spa is a hot bath or spring
standard abbreviation for son, placed after the bath

explanation.surface: A nanny holding a little boy after his warm bath turns out to be utterly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: Aia is the less common spelling of ayah. Aspasia, the famous companion of Pericles, gives her name to a charming, accomplished woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists aspasia as a term for a fascinating, cultivated woman, after the celebrated Greek courtesan.

clue.text: Item a Venetian restaurant served up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: trat is a short informal word for a trattoria, an Italian eatery

explanation.surface: Asks what dish an Italian restaurant in Venice might bring out.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi-&lit: the whole clue also describes the answer, a pastry that such a restaurant could serve as a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is one item on a menu, a pastry case with a filling.

clue.text: Old general, one with a tight hold reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the phrase is judged by its spoken sound

blocks.note: something that grips tightly, said without sounding the final r

explanation.surface: Describes a veteran commander known for his firm grip.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match works for non-rhotic speakers, who drop the final r of gripper.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman general who won the battle of Actium for Augustus.

clue.text: Muse about painting that's turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up means it now reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: an oil is a painting in oils
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: An artist's inspiration concerns a picture that has just appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over history.

clue.text: Hard working men on song getting fees paid voluntarily

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
a machine that is on is working
other ranks, ordinary soldiers
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Tough manual labourers who sing at their work earn freely given payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Honoraria are payments made for professional services where no fee is legally required, a plural Latin form.

clue.text: First-class part of Sunday Times? Go Mephisto!

blocks.note: A is the top grade, first-class
a newspaper is made up of pages

explanation.surface: A cheer for the crossword's top-quality slot in the Sunday paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as encouragement for the puzzle; the definition is a dismissal of the devil whose name the puzzle bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Apage is a Greek-derived command meaning get thee hence, used as in apage Satana, so it tells the devil to depart.

clue.text: One part of company showing skill

blocks.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
abbreviation for department, a division of a firm

explanation.surface: A single division of a firm demonstrates talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept is an adjective meaning skilled and proficient at some task.

clue.text: Sterility in skunk one accepted

blocks.note: atoc is a South American skunk in Chambers
Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: Finding infertility in a skunk that was taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Atocia is a technical word for barrenness, the inability of a female to bear young, from Greek.

clue.text: Tailor bargained for twill fabric

indicators.note: to tailor is to cut and reshape, so the letters of the next word are refashioned

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A clothier haggled over a roll of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like the person doing the haggling, but it is a verb telling you to remake the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabardine is a tightly woven twill cloth, often of wool, used for raincoats.

clue.text: Yanks leaving Japan could be personnel in forces

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

blocks.note: yanks as a verb, sudden pulls
J is the international vehicle code for Japan

explanation.surface: Americans pulling out of Japan might be military staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' suggests Americans; it is the verb meaning sharp tugs. Erk is British slang, chiefly RAF, for a lowly aircraftman or ground crew member.
explanation.definitionFit: Erks are low-ranking service members, especially RAF mechanics, so they are examples of forces personnel.

clue.text: Son with sporting wife gets depression

blocks.note: abbreviation for son
WAGs are the wives and girlfriends of sports stars

explanation.surface: A boy whose mother is a footballer's partner ends up feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG is British tabloid shorthand for the wives and girlfriends of footballers. 'Depression' suggests low mood; it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A swag is a hollow or dip in land, a geographical depression.

clue.text: Doctor leading is what serves as a model

blocks.note: to load dice is to doctor or tamper with them
the star is the leading performer

explanation.surface: A physician in charge is a good example to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning to falsify, not a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: A loadstar, a variant of lodestar, is a guiding star and so figuratively an example or ideal to follow.

clue.text: Small dish is timeless Portuguese fake

indicators.note: without time means the letter standing for time is dropped

blocks.note: abbreviation for Portuguese
a ringer is an impostor or fraudulent substitute

explanation.surface: A little plate is an ageless forgery from Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: A porringer is a small bowl with a handle, for porridge or soup.

clue.text: Learning nothing about L-shaped building material

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
zero, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Discovering nothing concerning a right-angled construction component.
explanation.definitionFit: Angle iron is steel bar rolled to a right-angled cross-section, used in building frames.

clue.text: Royals not normally seen around throne in Russian city

indicators.note: something done not in the normal way is disordered, so the letters are jumbled
seen around means placed so as to surround the next item

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
throne is slang for a lavatory seat, so a lav

explanation.surface: Unusually, monarchs are spotted beside a throne in some Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throne' pulls toward royalty in the surface; it is jokey slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaroslavl is an ancient city on the Volga, north-east of Moscow.

clue.text: Original cover, for instance for plants with tubers

blocks.note: OC is a collector's abbreviation, as in stamp collecting, for original cover
as in the sense of for example, such as

explanation.surface: A book's first jacket is cited as an example of something tuberous.
explanation.definitionFit: Oca is a South American wood sorrel grown for its edible tubers.

clue.text: One shoots wading bird on river?

blocks.note: a snipe is a long-billed marsh bird
abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Asks whether a shooter targets a marsh bird on a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a marksman comes from shooting snipe, a hard bird to hit, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who fires from cover, so someone who shoots.

clue.text: Prepare case of trout in English river

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are taken
in means placed inside the next item

blocks.note: outside letters of the fish
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Getting a trout ready inside a river in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare' here means to dress or clothe, as attire is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To attire someone is to dress them, getting them ready by clothing.

clue.text: Initiates an attack from the front in darts

indicators.note: in means one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: darts and spears are thrown weapons
the head is the front of a procession

explanation.surface: Someone opens an assault, starting at the front with thrown missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead an offensive is to lead it, so it begins the attack.

clue.text: Seals ostensibly are so brave when force unleashed

indicators.note: unleashed means set loose, so that letter is let go from the word

blocks.note: a brave person is without fear
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: Seals appear courageous once power is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: True seals are called earless seals because they lack external ear flaps; 'ostensibly' admits they do have inner ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals without visible ear flaps look as though they have no ears at all.

clue.text: See tar organised introduction of Microsoft Word on board

indicators.note: organised means arranged into order, so the letters are rearranged
an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the opening letter of the company

explanation.surface: Instructions to watch the tar sorted before introducing some Microsoft software on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Microsoft Word' fuses into the program's name, but Word belongs to the definition. Tar is also a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea term is a nautical expression, a word used aboard ship.

clue.text: Fruit unfortunately containing fish bone

indicators.note: containing means holding the next items within

blocks.note: alas is an exclamation of regret
the gar is a long-snouted fish
to bone is slang for to steal

explanation.surface: A sad tale of fruit found with a fishbone inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone' looks like a noun paired with fish; it is the slang verb meaning to pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Algarroba is the carob bean or mesquite pod, an edible fruit from a leguminous tree.

clue.text: Sounds like kind of coarse-grained rock

indicators.note: sounds like means judged on how it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: kind and nice both mean pleasant to others

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a particular type of rough stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as a type of rock; kind is the adjective meaning pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock with coarse grains of feldspar and quartz.

clue.text: Notes held in one song with tabla initially backing

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter of the word
backing means going backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a tune is a melody or song
the first letter of the Indian drum

explanation.surface: Sustained notes in a single song with an Indian drum accompanying.
explanation.walkthrough: A tabla is a pair of Indian hand drums; 'backing' looks like musical accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuti is the plural of tenuto, a musical direction for notes sustained for full value.

clue.text: Pamphlet found in vehicle or shed

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so those letters drop away

blocks.note: a farm vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaflet turned up in a car or a garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like an outbuilding; it is the verb meaning to discard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short treatise, often religious or political, issued as a pamphlet.

clue.text: Dry number first for Andy Williams?

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: sere means dried up
N for number, as in mathematics
opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A dry song to start off a crooner's set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Andy Williams' runs together as the American singer, but Andy only gives a letter and Williams is the definition; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Serena Williams is the tennis champion, so she is one example of a Williams.

clue.text: Champion of course forgoing golf range?

indicators.note: forgoing means doing without, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: Tiger Woods, champion of the golf course
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfing winner skipping the game to practise at a driving range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as naturally; it means of the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or rank, as is a range of seats or shelves set one above another.

clue.text: It's forbidden down under to eavesdrop on oriental mister

blocks.note: to tap a phone is to listen in secretly
U is a Burmese title of respect for a man

explanation.surface: Australians ban spying on a man from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Down under covers New Zealand here: tapu is the Maori word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapu is the Maori form of taboo, meaning sacred and forbidden.

clue.text: Time for bit of Waterfront in rock live from Edinburgh

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter
one thing for another means it takes the other's place
in shows where the swap takes place, inside the next word

blocks.note: abbreviation for time
first letter of the word
to rock is to sway to and fro

explanation.surface: A time for a stretch of waterfront within the rocky shore, live from Scotland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live from Edinburgh' sounds like a broadcast; it means the verb as used in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage, to stay somewhere means to live or reside there permanently.

clue.text: Fish live in Florida swamp

indicators.note: Chambers gives ransack as a sense of fish, and ransacking throws things into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Fish are alive in the swamps of Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' reads as the creatures living in the swamp, but it is the verb meaning to rummage. Vlei, from Dutch, is used in South Africa and in parts of the US for a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A vlei is a marsh or low wet ground; Chambers marks the swamp sense as American usage.

clue.text: Trifle: lovely to eat a piece

indicators.note: to eat is to take inside, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: a belle is a lovely woman
a + gat, slang for a gun or piece

explanation.surface: A dessert trifle that would be nice to eat a slice of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' and 'piece' suggest pudding; piece is gangster slang for a gun, as is gat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is something of little importance, just as a trifle is.

clue.text: Pale bubbly in vessel

blocks.note: a pale is a fence stake or post
cava is Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Wan fizz in a drinking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a container for the wine; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The postcava is the inferior vena cava, the great vein returning blood to the heart.

clue.text: Sun mess up getting press together

blocks.note: abbreviation for sun or Sunday
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A tabloid botches it, getting the newspapers in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and the press suggest newspapers; press is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Serr is an old word meaning to close up or crowd tightly, as ranks were serried.

clue.text: The west lacking leader not yet firm

indicators.note: without its leader means the opening letter is taken off

blocks.note: the west is where the sun sets, sunset direction

explanation.surface: The western world, without anyone in charge, is not yet stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete or jelly that is unset has not hardened yet.

clue.text: See Ireland's capital in summer? Not half a delightful place

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter, the first in the word
not half means only one half survives and the other is dropped
in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see
the country's opening letter
taken as written before halving

explanation.surface: Visit Dublin in summer? Not really a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like look at; Ely is the English cathedral city whose bishop's seat is a see.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium is the Greek paradise of the blessed, hence any place of perfect happiness.
